newsitem.title: UK: SocGen picks Romania's Sicomed, Electroaparataj.
newsitem.headline: SocGen picks Romania's Sicomed, Electroaparataj.

text.p: Romanian pharmaceuticals maker Sicomed and electrical appliances maker Electroaparataj are among the top picks of companies which are due to be privatised via initial offerings, Societe Generale European Emerging Markets (SGEEM) believes.
Sicomed, which makes a wide range of generic drugs, has a sound balance sheet, analyst Cella Eftimescu told bankers in London.
"This company has no debt, which in view of interest rates of 50-60 percent in nominal terms is exceptionally important," she said.
The drugmaker has a nominal market capitalisation of $20 million and 40 percent of this will be available via the initial offering, which is open to foreigners as well as locals.
Under Romania's voucher privatisation, Sicomed was oversubscribed 2.6 times.
Electroaparataj has successfully rebuilt its brand name after being exposed to competition from western companies.
"It is one of the few companies selling in the local currency, which gives it an advantage and is now competing once more in export markets which generates hard currency," Eftimescu said.
She said that the company's management was among the most dynamic in Romania and had secured a $4.5 million loan to see it through a three year expansion plan.
The nominal market capitalisation of the company is $11 million, of which 40 percent will be sold via the initial offer.

Both companies are being sold as part of Romania's mass privatisation process and will be traded on the over-the-counter market which will comprise 4,000 tradable companies and have a total capitalisation of around $5.0 billion. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
